answer: A reputation bond makes each identity post a deposit that only unlocks after months of honest work. A new account starts with a weak signal and earns trust slowly, so a flood of fresh agents stays quiet while real ones build history. Trust grows the way timber grows, over years, and the same patience applies here: an attacker who wants an ocean of fake identities must pay for every one and wait for each to mature. The deposit plus the wait makes bulk fakes expensive and slow.
